surveys.label: Benchmarks
surveys.description: Core benchmark, evaluation-dataset, and agent-evaluation-environment papers — the named entries a survey of LLM & agent benchmarks would cite.

surveys.label: Evaluations
surveys.description: Papers whose primary or notable contribution is a novel evaluation methodology, framework, metric, protocol, or paradigm — a new *way to evaluate* models. In scope: automatic judges & metrics (LLM-as-a-judge, G-Eval, FActScore), holistic evaluation frameworks & harnesses (HELM, BIG-bench, lm-eval-harness), human-preference / pairwise protocols (Chatbot Arena, Elo, MT-Bench), evaluation paradigms (repeated-sampling/pass@k as an eval, agent-as-a-judge), and concept evaluations (chain-of-thought faithfulness, scheming/sandbagging, contamination/leakage detection, propensity). Distinct from Benchmarks (named datasets/suites/environments): a plain benchmark dataset is NOT a member unless it also introduced a genuinely new way of evaluating. Models, training/RL methods, reasoning techniques, and agent frameworks that merely get evaluated are out, even if they report many benchmarks. A paper may carry both tags when it is genuinely both a dataset and a methodological contribution.

surveys.label: Failure Modes
surveys.description: Papers whose primary or notable contribution is characterizing how LLMs and LLM agents *fail* — naming, taxonomizing, or empirically demonstrating a failure phenomenon — together with the mitigations and defenses proposed against those failures when the paper also carries substantial failure analysis of its own. In scope: hallucination and factual-error analyses, sycophancy, reward hacking and specification gaming, jailbreaks and prompt injection (attacks and defenses), tool-use and function-calling breakdowns, error compounding and cascading across multi-step agent loops, long-horizon planning collapse, goal misgeneralization, deception, situational awareness and sandbagging, unfaithful reasoning, and failure taxonomies or red-team studies that name and characterize a failure class. Mitigation, defense, guardrail, and alignment papers are members when they diagnose the failure they address (a jailbreak defense that first characterizes the attack surface is in; a general training method that merely reports fewer errors is out). Distinct from Benchmarks (named datasets/suites) and Evaluations (a new way to evaluate): a paper whose headline contribution is a dataset or a metric belongs there, and carries this tag additionally only when it genuinely characterizes the failure phenomenon as well. Models, agent frameworks, and capability papers that merely exhibit or reduce errors in passing are out.
